messages:
samir: Heads-up — our canary traffic for ads-model:v2 in eu-west-1 is oscillating. Flux keeps re-applying the traffic-splitter and the UI shows 10% -> 90% -> 10% every ~30s. Seen this during the 03:10 deploy window.

olivia: :eyes: any error in the reconciler or the canary controller logs?

samir: Reconciler shows helm hook timeouts, and the traffic CRD shows conflicting controllers writing. Paste from flux: 
```
ts=2026-05-05T03:10:12Z caller=server.go:123 component=server event="reconcile start" name=ads-model-canary
err="helm post-install hook failed: timeout waiting for hook completion"
```
Also saw the envoy service traffic-split resource reported by the progressive-delivery controller as "unavailable endpoints" intermittently.

matt: another clue — cluster-autoscaler log shows node pool eu-gpu-pool scaled down by 1 at 03:09:57 (preemptible-like behavior). Canary pod landed on the new node and failed liveness for ~20s. That might've tripped the traffic controller health check so it reset the split and then flux re-applied helm w/ hook which then timed out when pods flapped.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaledown event: eu-gpu-pool-3 -> desired=2 (reason=scale-down, from=3) at 2026-05-05T03:09:57Z

jen: So this is a race: autoscaler scales down -> pod moves -> health flaps -> progressive controller thinks canary failed -> traffic flips -> GitOps reconcile reapplies helm chart -> helm waits for hooks which also time out because the node is still stabilizing.

kevin: Agreed. Two fixes: 1) make the canary health probe less sensitive (increase initialDelay/readiness thresholds) 2) guard the progressive rollouts against infra events (pause on node pool scaling or GPU evictions).

olivia: For immediate mitigation can we pause the rollout so traffic is stable for customers? Also revert to v1 until we patch.

samir: I paused the Canary in the progressive-delivery CR (set spec.paused=true) and bumped traffic back to 100% v1 via a quick flux patch. Command used locally: 
```
flux reconcile kustomization infra/canaries --with-source
kubectl patch traffic-split ads-service -p '{"spec":{"backends":[{"revision":"v1","weight":100}]}}' --type=merge
```
Traffic stabilized within 40s.

matt: Good catch. For the root cause we should: 
- increase liveness/readiness for GPU-backed pods (longer startup + backoff)
- remove expensive helm post-install hooks that block reconcile (move to pre-commit job in CI)
- add a gate in the canary controller to detect concurrent nodepool scale events

jen: I'll open a repo PR to move the hook out of the chart and add probe changes. I'll also add a small controller patch that reads cluster events (ScaleDown) and marks canary as "deferred" for 2m.

kevin: Also add a terraform guard: when scaling down GPU node pools require a min-available annotation so we don't drop below the number of running model replicas for any active canary. We should tie this to the rollout engine to prevent flips caused by infra-driven pod churn.

olivia: Can someone add a runbook entry? this pattern will repeat when we run capacity reclaim tests.

samir: I'll draft a short runbook: steps to pause canary, revert traffic, and patch flux if helm hooks block. Putting a TODO linking the PRs.

jen: PRs: 
- infra/helm-remove-hooks #542 (moves post-install work to CI)
- services/ads-model #221 (probe tweaks + grace period)
- rollout/controller #88 (defer on scale events)

matt: We should also add an alert: "canary-flip-flop" when traffic-split changes > 30% twice in 1m, routed to eng-oncall.

kevin: I'll create the alert and a terraform change request for nodepool min-available.

olivia: Follow-up meeting? 11:00 UTC to align on rollout hardening.

samir: Thanks — closing here once PRs are up. Will post link to the runbook and the revert commit. :thumbsup:
